items.excerpt: Wonder Dynamics co-founder Nikola Todorovic breaks down Autodesk Flow Studio's new 3D Editor + Canvas, which pairs interactive 3D scene construction — characters, mocap, camera tracks, Gaussian-splat environments from World Labs' Marble — with generative 2D video models. The pitch is directable AI filmmaking: block and light the shot in 3D, then finish it in a node-based 2D canvas rather than prompting a whole movie.

A coalition convened by Kathleen Kennedy and AFI dean Susan Ruskin went public with "Human Generative Workflows," a framework that gives the industry a shared vocabulary for authorship under generative AI. It explicitly separates craft-level AI assists — upscaling, sharpening, markerless mocap, a Resolve color assist — from prompted synthetic performances that substitute for human creative work.

Lineo, built by working commercial producers, launches a single production-management platform covering bid-to-wrap: AICP/APA budgets, calendars, bid packages, POs, payroll and petty cash with live actuals. AI drafts bid letters, parses and logs receipts and POs, and a built-in Production Assistant answers plain-language questions about the job's own data.

Artlist sold filmmakers a year of "unlimited" Seedance 2.5 generation for $500, then capped it roughly a week later, offering a credit upgrade as remedy. CineD argues the episode is a warning about building a production pipeline on resold frontier-model access whose economics can change overnight.

Busan's Asian Contents & Film Market unveiled its InnoAsia lineup, pairing Google DeepMind, Amazon Web Services and Kling AI with seven Korean startups, plus a branded-film contest with Hanwha and Innocean. It is one of the clearest signals yet of generative video vendors embedding themselves in Asian film-market infrastructure.

Animaze Montreal revealed 2026 programming (Sept 17–19) including its first-ever AI Animation Forum, alongside masterclasses from Bill Plympton and Johnnie Semerad. The festival is putting a hand-drawn-legend track and an AI pipeline track on the same schedule.

Abigail Hing Wen's directorial debut 'The Vale – Origins' is a hybrid animated/live-action short about a five-year-old who draws his way out of grief, and parents who rebuild his sketches as an AI-powered virtual sanctuary. Notably, the film about AI was made without it — a pointed craft position from a first-time director.

The insult "indie slop" has migrated from video-game discourse into film criticism, collapsing AI anxiety, market glut and contempt for amateur work into one word. IndieWire traces how the slur now gets aimed at low-budget human filmmaking that merely looks cheap.

Curious Refuge tests a free AI video generator that they argue has quietly closed much of the quality gap with paid frontier models. The walkthrough is aimed at filmmakers deciding where free tiers now fit in a shot-production workflow.

Theoretically Media puts two unreleased, codenamed AI video models through filmmaker-style tests and pairs the results with a free cinematic reference library. A useful read on what the next generation of text-to-video is actually good at shot-by-shot.
